pl-l3d20c5-d1e117.summary: States that Christ is priest and also victim and price of our reconciliation, offering himself on the altar of the cross not to the devil but to God the Trinity, for all as to the sufficiency of the price, but only for the elect as to efficacy, since he effected salvation only for the predestined. He is said to be handed over by the Father, by himself, by Judas, and by the Jews: by himself because he went willingly to the passion; by the Father because he suffered by the will of the Father, indeed of the whole Trinity; by Judas betraying; by the Jews instigating.
claims: Christ is priest, victim, and price.
Christ offered himself to the Trinity, not to the devil.
Christ died for all in sufficiency, for the elect in efficacy.
Christ was handed over by the Father, himself, Judas, and the Jews.

pl-l3d20c5-d1e120.summary: Distinguishes the acts: the act of Judas and the Jews was evil, that of Christ and the Father good; the work of Christ and the Father was good because their will was good; that of Judas and the Jews evil because their intention was evil. There were different acts or deeds, but one thing done, the passion itself.
claims: The acts of Judas and the Jews were evil; those of Christ and the Father good.
Different acts converge in one thing done, the passion.

pl-l3d20c5-d1e123.summary: Explains that the doctors sometimes join Father, Son, Judas, and the Jews in that deed, sometimes separate them: looking at the passion, they call it one work; attending to intentions and acts, they distinguish different deeds.
claims: The passion is one work but involves different deeds.

pl-l3d20c5-d1e127.summary: Cites Augustine: the handing over was done by the Father, by the Son, by Judas, one thing done; what distinguishes them is that Father and Son did it in charity, Judas in betrayal. We must consider not what a man does but with what will. In the same deed we bless God and detest Judas, since God thought of our salvation, Judas of the price he sold the Lord for, the Son of the price he gave for us. Different intention makes different deeds, though there is one thing from different ones.
claims: What matters morally is the will, not the outward deed.
Different intentions make different deeds in one thing done.

pl-l3d20c5-d1e136.summary: Concludes that Augustine says there was one thing and different deeds: one passion, different acts; the acts of Judas and the Jews by which they worked Christ's passion were evil, while the passion itself is good and the work of God.
claims: The passion is good and God's work, though worked through evil acts.

pl-l3d20c5.summary: Teaches that Christ is priest, victim, and price of our reconciliation, offering himself on the cross not to the devil but to God the Trinity, for all as to sufficiency of the price but only for the elect as to efficacy. He was handed over by the Father, by himself, by Judas, and by the Jews: by himself, going willingly; by the Father, by the will of the whole Trinity; by Judas betraying; by the Jews instigating. The act of Judas and the Jews was evil, that of Christ and the Father good; there were different acts but one thing done, the passion. Augustine: what distinguishes them is the will, charity versus betrayal; different intentions make different deeds in one thing.
claims: Christ is priest, victim, and price of our reconciliation.
Christ offered himself to the Trinity, not to the devil.
Christ died for all as to sufficiency, for the elect as to efficacy.
The Father, Christ, Judas, and the Jews all handed Christ over, with different wills.
One thing done can involve different acts, good and evil, according to intention.
